parsed.study_design: Cross-sectional resident survey with interviews and economic modeling
parsed.population_and_sample: 135 adult residents of Providenciales, recruited digitally and in person between May and December 2025
parsed.exposure: Water-service arrangements and institutional conditions, including Provo Water connection, delivery method, distribution coverage, service shutoffs, cistern-refill service, and current water source
parsed.outcome: Difficulty obtaining water, service interruptions and empty-cistern days, water-source satisfaction, preferred access mode, willingness to pay for uninterrupted in-home piped water, and willingness to use recycled wastewater
parsed.rationale: The Methods section (pp. 18–21) reports an IRB-approved cross-sectional resident survey, stakeholder interviews, regression analyses, and economic modeling. The survey and Results (pp. 22–31; Appendix 1) empirically relate utility connection, delivery arrangements, shutoffs, and cistern refilling to household water access, reliability, satisfaction, and affordability-related outcomes. The Background section on “Water Shortages and Distribution on Provo” (pp. 14–15) also identifies institutionally patterned gaps in Provo Water's distribution coverage, including unconnected low-income communities.
